name: Bone pain
description: Bone pain is a deep, aching, or throbbing pain localised to bone, often worse at night and not relieved by rest. In an oncology context, it is a key symptom of bone metastases (most commonly from breast, prostate, lung, kidney, and thyroid primaries), primary bone tumours (osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma), and multiple myeloma. Cancer-related bone pain is caused by periosteal stretching, cytokine-mediated sensitisation, or pathological fracture. New or worsening localised bone pain in a known cancer patient or a patient with constitutional symptoms requires urgent imaging to exclude metastatic disease or pathological fracture.
